patch.value: GH-1773: refusal envelopes echo URL userinfo when it contains whitespace and a percent-encoded @ separator

GH-1773 (filed 2026-11-23 from the pm-rust parity review, reproduced on the pinned pm-cli oracle; native and TS behave the same). A refusal envelope echoes an open blocker's title verbatim. When that title holds a URL whose userinfo contains whitespace and a percent-encoded @ (https://fixture:fake words%40example.invalid/path), the userinfo is not masked: pm start-task sample-one --json refused by that blocker prints 'fixture:fake words'. Expected: credential-shaped URL userinfo is masked in every refusal and diagnostic projection, whitespace-bearing userinfo and an encoded separator included, matching the masking of plain user:pass@host; plain masking unchanged. Duplicate check: searched redaction URL userinfo whitespace percent-encoded separator refusal envelope; pm-gh1707 (closed) fixed public-URL @-in-path over-redaction and claim-refusal echoes, pm-nhauur and pm-5htunt (closed) cover other echo surfaces, none covers whitespace plus encoded separators.

A redaction corpus case covers whitespace in userinfo with a percent-encoded separator, applied to refusal envelopes, diagnostics and JSON and TOON output; Plain user:pass@host masking and public URLs with @ in the path are unchanged
Credential-shaped URL userinfo is masked in refusals and diagnostics whatever whitespace or encoding it carries

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Root cause and fix (2026-11-23): redactUrlCredentialsInText judged each whitespace-delimited word alone, so a stored title holding a URL whose password contains a blank split into a scheme word with a colon but no at sign and a host word with an at sign (or its percent escape) but no colon; neither word matched the token rule. The plain at-sign form leaked the same way, not only the encoded one, and Node's WHATWG URL parser reads that spelling as userinfo with a spaced password. Fix in src/core/shared/url-credentials.ts: before the word rule, a word with no at sign that opens a URL authority with a user-colon prefix (scheme, one or two slashes, a colon that port digits alone never follow, no path, no bracketed IPv6 host) is joined across any whitespace with the later words up to the first that holds an at sign or its escape, within 16 words and 512 code units and before another URL starts, and the joined span goes through redactUrlCredentialsInToken. Line breaks and tabs count as blanks because URL parsers drop them. Host-and-port and plain-host prose before a later at sign stays intact. Every outbound surface (refusal guidance in JSON and text, telemetry sanitizeString, Sentry scrubbing) already routes free text through this one function. Verified end to end in a sandbox: a start-task refusal gated by such a blocker now prints the scheme, the placeholder and the host only, in JSON and TOON output.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Rework after Codex review round 1 (2026-11-23, 8 URL findings). The opening word may now hold its own separator (an encoded at sign inside the password), skips any number of authority slashes, ignores a colon that only appears in a query or fragment, exempts only a real host:port head (a label run, a colon and at least one digit), and also opens on a single dotless label when a later word carries the user-password colon (a spaced username). The continuation takes the LAST at sign or its escape that starts within 16 words and 512 code units, as a URL parser takes the authority's last at sign; the word holding it may run past the length bound (a long query), and a word that starts another URL or holds a path delimiter before any separator ends the search. All 8 reproductions are pinned in tests/unit/core/shared/url-credentials.spec.ts, and the earlier prose and bound cases still pass.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 2 (2026-11-23): a redirect URL in the final word's query stopped the scan before its separator (now only a scheme at the end of the text before the first path delimiter starts another URL, read back from the colon, which also removes the quadratic unanchored scheme search Codex measured); a dotted spaced username and a password starting with digits were not joined (any colon-bearing head that is no dotted or localhost host:port now opens, and a dotless or dotted label opens when a later word carries a colon with text after it); a quoted URL followed by prose with a colon was over-redacted (a quote, backtick or angle bracket in the authority ends it). Declined with reason: preserving the host and path after a join — the single-token rule masks through the last at sign by design (GH-1707, base64 passwords hold slashes), and the joined span is pinned to redact exactly as the same URL without blanks.

value.text: Greptile review round 1 (2026-11-23, P1): a tab right after the authority slashes split the URL before its username, so no opening word was found and the spaced password survived. A word that ends with its authority slashes is now a pending opening whose authority starts in the next word, judged as if the blank between them were dropped (URL parsers drop tabs and line breaks there); prose with a bare scheme is still left alone.

value.text: Codex review round 3 and Greptile round 2 (2026-11-24): the scheme separator is the first colon that authority slashes follow, so a compact JSON field name before the URL is skipped; a quote, backtick or angle bracket ends the URL only when it directly precedes the scheme (an apostrophe inside a password is data); a label opening may hold percent escapes (only an at sign or its escape is excluded); a password colon that a tab or line break follows counts, a clock time never does, and a colon that a space follows counts only when the separator's host goes on into a path (URL-shaped, never an email address); an encoded at sign that starts inside the 512-unit bound is read whole; the host:port check runs only on a DNS-length head, so an 8M-character dotted host no longer overflows the regex stack inside the redactor.

patch.value: Credential-shaped URL userinfo is masked in every refusal and diagnostic projection whatever whitespace or encoding it carries, and plain user:pass@host masking is unchanged

redactUrlCredentialsInText now joins a URL whose userinfo holds blanks into one word before the word rule runs: a word opens a join at the last scheme separator that authority slashes follow when its authority holds a non host:port colon, or is a single label whose password colon comes later (never a clock time; a colon that a space follows only before a host with a path or inside a URL its quote closes), or ends with its slashes (a tab follows); it is joined through the later word holding the authority's last at sign or its escape within 16 words and 512 code units, stops at another URL, a path delimiter or the URL's closing delimiter, and the joined span is redacted exactly as the same URL without blanks. Windows drives, Markdown links, quoted URLs and public host-and-port prose stay intact. The start-task refusal from the issue now prints only the scheme, the placeholder and the host in JSON and text output. Review: Codex rounds 1 to 5, Greptile rounds 1 to 4 and CodeRabbit round 1 addressed; residuals recorded on pm-jcz7qz.

The issue reproduction, the plain at-sign variant and every review-round leak are masked idempotently; plain masking and public URLs with an at sign in the path are unchanged, and prose cases stay intact
URL userinfo that holds whitespace and a plain or percent-encoded at sign is masked in refusals, diagnostics, telemetry and Sentry text
